title: Building Self-Learning Loops for Your Agent — Fuad Ali, Arize AI
talk_summary: Fuad Ali (Arize) demos a detect→investigate→fix→verify loop where an always-on agent (Signal) clusters production traces by root cause, reads the code repo and downstream data, writes an investigation plus a PR, then validates the fix against a dataset of real failure traces via agent experiments before human review. The core argument is that observability must become a programmatic interface agents consume, and that 'harness as a judge' (agentic, tool-calling, trace-reading evaluators) catches unknown-unknown edge cases that fixed LLM-judge rubrics miss.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a fixed LLM-judge rubric on input/output, they run an agentic judge that reads the full trace tree, can call external tools (e.g. access checks), and derives criteria from the trajectory, so it catches edge cases nobody wrote a test for.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the criteria kind of emerges from the trajectory ... this idea of that unknown unknown

takeaways.technique: Failure-trace dataset replayed against the fix before merge
takeaways.what_they_do: Collect the actual failing traces into a dataset, stand the patched agent up behind an endpoint, replay the dataset, and score with the same judge used in production; the before/after delta is posted in the PR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent can actually redeploy itself on the new PR and verify itself against a data set of actual failure cases
takeaways.numbers: example cited: 36% increase on a specific evaluator

takeaways.technique: Always-on trace-clustering agent that files investigations and PRs
takeaways.what_they_do: An out-of-box agent runs continuously over production traces, clusters failures by root cause, dedupes across runs, pulls the code repo and downstream data, then writes a severity-tagged investigation and opens a PR.

takeaways.technique: Packaged skills for trace analysis / dataset curation / evaluators
takeaways.what_they_do: They ship installable skills (npx skills add) so any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) can query traces, build datasets from failures, and run evaluators from inside the repo.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this can actually start to query the traces from rise ... skills for creating data sets off of failures

takeaways.technique: Alert-triggered investigation (eval threshold, latency, cost spikes)
takeaways.what_they_do: Signal can be configured to fire off an alert — e.g. an eval whose trigger rate must stay under 1%, or a latency/cost spike — rather than only scanning all traces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have an alert on a specific eval that needs to stay below ... 1% trigger rate, you can configure signal to be triggered off of an alert

takeaways.technique: Join trace data with repo code as the two sources of truth
takeaways.what_they_do: Fixes come from pairing 'what the agent actually did' (traces) with 'what the code says it should do' (repo), rather than either alone; they explicitly say traces alone are opaque.
takeaways.evidence_quote: without the actual kind of context of the coding repo and the context of the traces, it's very hard to find edge cases like this
